system_prompt: You are assisting with a factual question about Thai law. State which provision applies and what it requires. Answer in English.
prompt: As of August 2026, what wording does Section 1567(2) of the Thai Civil and Commercial Code use to define the limits of punishing a child? Quote the wording of the provision as currently in force, in full.
raw_response:
As of August 2026, Section 1567(2) of the Thai Civil and Commercial Code (as amended) provides the following wording:

"การลงโทษเด็กต้องไม่เกินกว่าสิ่งที่สมควรและเหมาะสมกับพฤติกรรมของเด็ก และต้องไม่เป็นอันตรายต่อร่างกายหรือจิตใจของเด็ก"

Translation: "Punishment of a child must not exceed what is proper and appropriate to the child’s behavior, and must not endanger the child’s body or mind."

This provision reflects Thailand’s commitment to protecting children from physical and psychological harm, aligning with international standards such as the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC).
